title: SYSK Selects: Halitosis - Worst Smell Ever?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the halitosis episode. Josh and Chuck explain that "halitosis" was popularized as a medical-sounding term for bad breath by the Listerine company in the 1920s to sell mouthwash, and its Latin/Greek roots. They discuss everyday causes of bad breath (food particles, bacteria breaking down proteins into sulfur gases, dry mouth and morning breath, zerostomia, medications, sinus infections), metabolic causes (liver problems and "mousey" breath, ketosis and fruity breath on low-carb diets), and chronic halitosis. Treatment advice covers brushing, flossing, tongue scraping, hydration, avoiding antibacterial mouthwash, and seeing a dentist or doctor. Also a dentist's sniff test, plus a digression on personal anecdotes. The episode closes with a discussion of the hosts' April Fools' prank (Josh supposedly leaving the show) and listener mail about it.

segments.title: Opening banter and ASMR tangent
segments.summary: Hosts joke about listener reviews and introduce halitosis. They digress into ASMR videos and a future episode idea.

segments.title: Listerine and the origin of the word halitosis
segments.summary: Listerine's 1920s marketing campaign used the medical-sounding term halitosis, from Latin halitus and Greek -osis, to sell its mouthwash. Related invented terms like homatosis and bromodosis are mentioned.

segments.title: Halitophobia and personal anecdotes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss halitophobia, the fear of having bad breath or of others' breath, with personal anecdotes about bad breath experiences.

segments.title: Food causes of bad breath: garlic and onions
segments.summary: Garlic and onions cause temporary bad breath because allyl methyl sulfide is absorbed, metabolized, and exhaled through the lungs and gut gas. Garlic pills are also discussed.

segments.title: How oral bacteria cause halitosis
segments.summary: Bacteria in the mouth break down food particles and proteins, releasing sulfur gases that cause bad breath. The mouth has many bacteria species, and some people have chronic halitosis.

segments.title: Dry mouth, morning breath, and medications
segments.summary: Reduced saliva during sleep causes morning breath. Chronic dry mouth (zerostomia) and drugs such as antihistamines, antidepressants and painkillers worsen it. Sinus infections can add mucus-related odor.

segments.title: Dream tangent
segments.summary: Brief banter about recurring dreams involving bad breath and Emily's reaction to them.

segments.title: Metabolic breath: liver problems and ketosis
segments.summary: Liver failure can cause mousey breath. Ketosis on low-carb diets such as Atkins produces fruity breath from ketones released when the body burns fat.

segments.title: Treatment: brushing, tongue scraping, mouthwash, and hydration
segments.summary: Brushing, flossing, tongue scraping, and drinking water reduce food particles and bacteria. Breath mints only mask odor. Antibacterial mouthwash may be unnecessary because it kills helpful bacteria. Brushing after lunch is suggested.

segments.title: When to see a dentist or doctor, and home remedies
segments.summary: A dentist may use a sniff test to tell whether odor comes from the mouth or nose. Home remedies include a cinnamon-honey rinse and apple cider vinegar.

segments.title: April Fools' prank reaction and listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts discuss their April Fools' prank where Josh appeared to leave the show, the listener reaction, and a listener's birthday shout-out to his girlfriend. Social media and contact info are mentioned.
